scenes.title: 1874 Breslau Clinic: 26-Year-Old Carl Wernicke Testing Object Pointing vs Fluent Paraphasic Speech Beside His Two-Hub Brain Sketch

layout.description: Sunlit 1874 European hospital consultation room with a clean oak desk holding three simple everyday objects (a silver key, a water glass, and a hairbrush), a tuning bell proving intact hearing, and Carl Wernicke's hand-drawn 1874 left-hemisphere wiring diagram linking posterior temporal 'a1' to frontal 'b' via an arcuate fiber curve.

positions.who: Carl Wernicke (26-year-old mannequin in 1874 physician frock coat and spectacles)
positions.where: gently ringing a small desk bell behind the patient (she turns instantly!) then asking verbally 'Please hand me the key' while gesturing NOT at all with his eyes

positions.who: Patient Susanne Adam (59-year-old mannequin in neat 1874 shawl and dress)
positions.where: speaking animatedly with warm, natural hand gestures and fluent cadence while reaching uncertainly past the key toward the hairbrush

props.name: three-object comprehension tray (key, water glass, hairbrush) & desk bell
props.period_detail: bell proves intact hearing; verbal-only request exposes lost spoken-word comprehension

props.name: Wernicke's 1874 hand-inked 'a1 -> b' cortical network diagram
props.period_detail: the historic sketch connecting posterior temporal sensory hub to Broca's frontal motor hub

actions.verb_sequence: taps the soft desk bell out of sight -> Patient turns briskly proving normal hearing -> Wernicke asks verbally for the key -> Patient replies in smooth, rhythmic, cheerful sentences yet picks up the brush
switches to a friendly visual mime of unlocking a door -> Patient nods immediately in clear visual understanding and hands him the key!

reactions.reaction: relaxes warmly once visual demonstration bypasses the broken acoustic-word decoder
traces the posterior temporal hub and connecting fiber arc on his 1874 diagram

scenes.wardrobe: 1874 German medical frock coat, high collar, cravat; modest 19th-century wool shawl over buttoned dress.
scenes.lighting: Bright high-key European hospital window light.
scenes.recognition_hook: She hears a quiet bell across the room and speaks in smooth, musical sentences — yet spoken words land like an unknown language until you mime unlocking a door.

key_visual.description: an 1874 physician at a sunlit clinic desk with a key, glass, and brush tray plus a hand-drawn two-hub brain diagram testing a fluently speaking seated patient

scenes.title: Predicting 'Conduction Aphasia' Before Seeing the Tract

layout.description: Warm sunlit desk where Wernicke draws a small red 'X' strictly across the connecting pathway between intact Hub A1 (temporal) and intact Hub B (frontal).

positions.where: drawing the predicted third syndrome: Understands YES, Speaks Fluently YES, Repeats Aloud NO!

props.name: 3-column syndrome prediction chart (Broca / Wernicke / Conduction)
props.period_detail: deduced a real neurological disorder from circuit logic alone

actions.verb_sequence: inks the fiber-cut prediction between temporal and frontal centers

reactions.reaction: marvels as real bedside conduction-aphasia cases confirm his sketch

scenes.recognition_hook: Just like Mendeleev predicting undiscovered elements from gaps in the periodic table, 26-year-old Wernicke predicted a new brain syndrome from a wiring sketch.

scenes.title: 2015 MRI Upgrade: Sound Monitor vs Semantic Meaning Network

layout.description: Clean bright neuroimaging suite comparing posterior STG phonological monitoring against broader middle/anterior temporal meaning hubs.

positions.where: overlaying hundreds of stroke MRIs to separate sound-form decoding (pSTG) from conceptual meaning (MTG/angular gyrus)

props.name: Dual-Stream Dorsal/Ventral language map
props.period_detail: resolves 140 years of textbook drift over where 'Wernicke's Area' sits

actions.verb_sequence: highlights pSTG self-monitor loop vs ventral middle-temporal meaning hub

scenes.recognition_hook: Modern MRI proved Wernicke's spot is your voice's live headphone monitor — while word meanings spread across a wider temporal neighborhood.

scenes.title: Visual Pictures & Gestures: Communicating Respectfully After Receptive Stroke

layout.description: Sunlit rehab table with crisp photo communication cards, written keywords, and calm gestures.

positions.where: communicating smoothly using picture cards and clear visual context instead of raising voice volume

props.name: visual communication board
props.period_detail: routes intact visual meaning straight past damaged auditory phoneme decoding

actions.verb_sequence: points to clear visual card while speaking calmly -> Patient nods and points accurately

scenes.recognition_hook: Speaking LOUDER never fixes Wernicke's aphasia — pairing calm speech with visual pictures and gestures opens the side door immediately.
